title: Carl Jung's scarab beetle as a time loop

tellings.quote: Carl Young had this patient who was completely kind of materialist and inaccessible not woo woo at all and she comes in and she goes you know I had this weird dream last night it was this this golden scarab beetle was given to me as a gift
she says look I had I had this dream last night that I was gifted this golden scare Beetle
tellings.difference: Told as a story from therapy, with no time-loop framing; dated to the early 20th century.
tellings.link_reason: Same story of Jung's materialist patient dreaming of a golden scarab, told by the same host.

as_told.title: Jung's patient and the golden scarab beetle

tellings.quote: But she's very skeptical. And as she's telling the story, a scarab beetle comes down the window sill and lands right in the office.
tellings.difference: Describes the beetle arriving at the window while she tells the dream, and does not frame it as a time loop.
tellings.link_reason: Both are Michels telling Jung's anecdote of the skeptical patient and the golden scarab beetle.

as_told.title: Carl Jung's patient and the golden scarab beetle

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a story about Carl Jung, a famous psychiatrist, and one of his patients, a very down-to-earth woman who did not believe in anything mystical. According to Michels, she told Jung she had dreamed of being given a golden scarab beetle as a gift. Michels frames this as a kind of time loop, which would mean events can reach backwards or forwards in time in ways we do not usually accept.
